How does a prince who just lost a war beat the Mongols, one of the most feared armies on Earth, without spending a fortune?
This is the story of how Majapahit was born.
In 1292, Jayakatwang of Kediri attacks the kingdom of Singhasari and kills its king.
The king's son-in-law, Raden Wijaya, escapes, then bows to Jayakatwang and pretends to surrender.
He is given a patch of forest called Tarik, where his men find maja fruit so bitter it makes them gag.
Quietly, the new village becomes his base, named after that fruit: Majapahit.
Meanwhile, about a thousand ships carrying some twenty thousand Mongol troops arrive on Java.
Kublai Khan sent them to punish Singhasari's king, who had insulted his envoy.
But that king is already dead, and the Mongols have no idea that Jayakatwang rules Java now.
Raden Wijaya sees a golden opportunity.
He sends the Mongol commanders an offer they can't refuse.
Your enemy is in Kediri, he says. Let's take him down together!
Wijaya's fighters and the Mongol troops march side by side and storm Kediri.
Jayakatwang's army falls apart, and the king himself is captured.
The Mongols celebrate their easy victory, lay down their weapons, and start to relax.
That's exactly what Wijaya was waiting for.
He asks to return home to prepare gifts for Kublai Khan, then turns on his allies.
His forces ambush the Mongol escort and launch a surprise attack on their camp.
The Mongols are shocked, they lose thousands of soldiers, and they run for their ships.
They sail back to China empty handed, and Kublai Khan never conquers Java.
In 1293, Raden Wijaya is crowned the first king of Majapahit.
His kingdom would grow into one of the greatest empires in the history of the archipelago.
Sometimes, a war isn't won by the biggest army, but by the smartest strategy.
